recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. A future source change would require a new work-group decision to make empty-trigger topics invalid, add an invariant, or alter server create-time validation expectations.
issue_request: FHIR-33674 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked what happens when the then-current resourceTrigger and eventTrigger elements were both absent, with final guidance that such SubscriptionTopic resources simply will not trigger, that extension or otherwise non-triggering topics remain possible, and that servers MAY reject triggering mechanisms they do not support.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 305bddee799e44657448bd138bcd4ccaebbcda1d, which added SubscriptionTopic narrative text explaining that topics without computable definitions are not expected to trigger unless a server explicitly supports them and that unsupported or non-computable mechanisms may be rejected. The SubscriptionTopic resource is active in source/fhir.ini.
additional_context: FHIR-46492 later collapsed SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger and SubscriptionTopic.eventTrigger into the current optional SubscriptionTopic.trigger backbone, so the original R4B element names no longer appear in current source. The current notes still state the relevant behavior in current terminology. FHIR-I WGM minutes record the FHIR-33674 Persuasive with Modification motion, and no relevant Zulip conflict was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-notes.xml text already states that topics without computable definitions are not expected to trigger unless explicitly supported, and that servers supporting create on SubscriptionTopic MAY reject resources lacking computable definitions or depending on unsupported mechanisms.
